findings.assertion: The Juárez administration's nationalization of ecclesiastical property (12 July 1859) and the secularization decree for hospitals and charities (2 February 1861) were separate measures, not one law.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM indexed reform-law list; dates under Gobierno de Benito Juárez
findings.limitations: Texts of both original decrees and local implementation in Mexico City have not been read; do not presume a particular hospital changed ownership on these dates

findings.assertion: The 1859 laws separately listed civil marriage (23 July) and civil registration (28 July), alongside the 12 July nationalization law; these chronology entries should not be collapsed into a generic single Reform Laws event.
findings.limitations: INEHRM listing accessed in index excerpt; official decrees, wording and application not inspected

findings.assertion: On the present Museo Nacional de Arte site, a former Jesuit college property completed in 1695 was reused as the Hospital de San Andrés beginning in November 1770; these dates concern predecessors of the current building.
findings.source_locator: INAH Lugares MUNAL building history, lines 29–31
findings.limitations: Narrative relates several earlier property uses; original plans and archival records uninspected

findings.assertion: The Hospital de San Andrés building was demolished in 1904; Silvio Contri designed its replacement as the Ministry of Communications and Public Works building, inaugurated in 1911. The existing MUNAL structure should not be presented as an intact eighteenth-century hospital.
findings.limitations: Demolition, technical design and inauguration documented in one institutional summary; original engineering and demolition files unexamined

findings.assertion: The Communications building housed the Archivo General de la Nación from 1973 to 1977 and was converted into the Museo Nacional de Arte in 1982.
findings.limitations: Institutional brief does not specify the extent of AGN occupation or renovation chronology; AGN records not examined

findings.assertion: Paseo de la Reforma's initial route was commissioned during Maximilian's Second Empire, prior to Porfirio Díaz's later expansions and monumental redesign; describing its creation as Porfirian erases the imperial origin.
findings.source_locator: UNAM journal abstract first paragraph; CCH UNAM city history sections on Maximilian and Porfiriato
findings.limitations: Journal full text not inspected; original 1864 plans and precise commission date need confirmation; source summaries not independent primary corroboration

findings.assertion: UNAM's historical synthesis dates replacement of gas street lighting with electric lighting to 1888 and electric streetcar inauguration to 1900, while distinguishing these projects from early imperial gas illumination.
findings.source_locator: CCH UNAM nineteenth-century Mexico City history, line 40
findings.limitations: Exact dates require independent contemporary engineering/concession sources; likely semantic overlap with earlier staged electric tram entries

findings.assertion: The UNAM urban-history overview contrasts improved central boulevards, illumination and transit with districts lacking basic sanitation, water and reliable transport during the late Porfiriato; infrastructural modernization was unevenly distributed.
findings.limitations: Specific neighborhood-level distribution needs archival maps and social history; avoid treating an educational synthesis as a primary survey
